title: Types
explain: Java has primitive types such as `int`, `double`, `boolean` and `char`, plus objects like `String`. `var` lets the compiler infer a local variable's type, but the variable is still strongly typed. Converting a larger type to a smaller one needs an explicit cast.
exercise: Declare one variable of each primitive type you know and print them, then divide two ints and two doubles and compare the results.
tip: Dividing two `int` values throws away the remainder. Make one operand a `double` when you want decimals.
